title: Rescale a bus-fleet model whose units were mixed

blocks.text: A city transit agency chooses which bus orders to place this year. A colleague built the model in `fleet.py` from three sources: order values in dollars from the finance system, the budget and the overdraft in $M from the board pack, and a switch row with $`M = 10^9`$. It gives the right plan, but its matrix spans more than nine powers of ten, which lesson 10.1.2 showed is outside the safe range.

The colleague's model, `build_raw()`, with $`J`$ the orders, $`p_j`$ and $`v_j`$ an order's price and value in dollars, $`B`$ the budget, $`L`$ the overdraft limit and $`F`$ the arrangement fee, all in dollars:

Write the rescaled model first, in this notation: every amount (the objective, the rows and the overdraft variable $`d`$) in $k, and the switch row's $`M`$ replaced by the smallest value the data make valid. Then write `build_scaled()` to build it, returning a `Fleet` with the same fields as `build_raw()`, the overdraft now in $k.

The tests fix a plan (which orders, the overdraft in $k, whether it is arranged), ask the solver whether it is allowed, and read its objective; they also check that the matrix span (largest absolute coefficient over smallest) is below 10,000. About eight lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

# Each order: (price, value), in dollars. Invented teaching data, not a real agency's.
ORDERS = {
    "electric": (4_200_000, 5_100_000),
    "hybrid": (2_600_000, 3_000_000),
    "diesel": (1_500_000, 1_650_000),
    "shuttle": (450_000, 520_000),
}
BUDGET = 7_000_000      # dollars
LIMIT = 900_000         # the most the overdraft may be, dollars
FEE = 150_000           # to arrange an overdraft, dollars


@dataclass
class Fleet:
    model: mathopt.Model
    buy: dict[str, mathopt.Variable]
    overdraft: mathopt.Variable
    arranged: mathopt.Variable


def build_raw() -> Fleet:
    """The colleague's model: objective in dollars, budget rows and overdraft in $M, M = 1e9."""
    model = mathopt.Model(name="fleet, mixed units")
    buy = {name: model.add_binary_variable(name=f"buy_{name}") for name in ORDERS}
    overdraft = model.add_variable(lb=0, name="overdraft")
    arranged = model.add_binary_variable(name="arranged")
    model.maximize(sum(value * buy[n] for n, (_, value) in ORDERS.items()) - FEE * arranged)
    model.add_linear_constraint(
        sum(price / 1e6 * buy[n] for n, (price, _) in ORDERS.items()) <= BUDGET / 1e6 + overdraft, name="budget")
    model.add_linear_constraint(overdraft <= LIMIT / 1e6, name="limit")
    model.add_linear_constraint(overdraft <= 1e9 * arranged, name="switch")
    return Fleet(model, buy, overdraft, arranged)


def build_scaled() -> Fleet:
    """The same model with every amount in $k, and the smallest valid M."""
    model = mathopt.Model(name="fleet, $k")
    buy = {name: model.add_binary_variable(name=f"buy_{name}") for name in ORDERS}
    overdraft = model.add_variable(lb=0, name="overdraft")
    arranged = model.add_binary_variable(name="arranged")
    model.maximize(sum(value / 1000 * buy[n] for n, (_, value) in ORDERS.items()) - FEE / 1000 * arranged)
    model.add_linear_constraint(
        sum(price / 1000 * buy[n] for n, (price, _) in ORDERS.items()) <= BUDGET / 1000 + overdraft, name="budget")
    model.add_linear_constraint(overdraft <= LIMIT / 1000, name="limit")
    smallest_valid_m = LIMIT / 1000      # the limit row already caps the overdraft here
    model.add_linear_constraint(overdraft <= smallest_valid_m * arranged, name="switch")
    return Fleet(model, buy, overdraft, arranged)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    fleet = build_scaled()
    result = mathopt.solve(fleet.model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS)
    print(result.termination.reason.name, result.objective_value())

import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from datetime import timedelta

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

from fleet import build_scaled

fleet = build_scaled()
sizes = [abs(row.get_coefficient(v)) for row in fleet.model.linear_constraints() for v in fleet.model.row_nonzeros(row)]
print("matrix span of the $k model:", round(max(sizes) / min(sizes), 1))

result = mathopt.solve(fleet.model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS, params=mathopt.SolveParameters(time_limit=timedelta(seconds=5)))
print("status:", result.termination.reason.name)
print("best value, $k:", round(result.objective_value(), 1))
print("orders bought:", sorted(n for n, v in fleet.buy.items() if result.variable_values(v) > 0.5))
print("overdraft, $k:", round(result.variable_values(fleet.overdraft), 1))

cases.says: a plan that overspends with an arranged overdraft is allowed, and the same plan with none arranged is refused, all amounts in $k
the rescaled model's matrix span is below 10,000, which takes a data-derived M as well as new units
the overdraft limit is converted to $k with the rest, so an overdraft above it is still refused
the objective is in $k, so a fixed plan's value is its value in thousands

origin.section: A Valid M Is Part of Scaling: Replace 1e9 With the Bound the Data Give

concepts: scaling a row, a column or the objective by a positive number keeps the allowed plans and the best plan
replacing a huge M by the bound the data give is the scaling step no change of units can make
